mc_1.prompt: Heavy rains are expected in 3 days. Your rice crop needs protection.
mc_1.voicePrompt: Heavy rains are expected in three days. What will you do?

mc_2a.prompt: The rains came but your insurance covered 80% of the damage. Great decision!
mc_2a.voicePrompt: The insurance covered 80% of the damage. Great decision!
mc_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Insurance Literacy] Crop insurance costs a small premium but protects you from losses 10x larger.

mc_2b.prompt: Your crop survived but now you owe ₹8,000 at 30% interest to the moneylender.
mc_2b.voicePrompt: Your crop survived, but you now owe 8,000 rupees to the moneylender.
mc_2b.lesson: Moneylenders charge 25-30% interest. Formal bank loans are only 7%. Always choose formal credit.

mc_2c.prompt: The rains destroyed 60% of your crop. Without insurance, you have no fallback.
mc_2c.voicePrompt: The rains destroyed 60% of your crop. Without insurance, you have no fallback.
mc_2c.lesson: Without savings or insurance, one bad season can push a family into poverty.

mp_1.prompt: Your wheat harvest is ready. A middleman offers ₹1,400/quintal. The mandi (market) price is ₹1,800 but you must transport it.
mp_1.voicePrompt: Your wheat harvest is ready. A middleman offers 1,400. Mandi price is 1,800. What will you do?

options.C: Store and wait for better price

mp_2a.prompt: You sold quickly and got ₹28,000. But you left ₹8,000 on the table by not going to the mandi.
mp_2a.lesson: [Skill Tested: Negotiation] Always compare prices at multiple buyers. The mandi price is publicly listed on e-NAM (National Agriculture Market app).

mp_2b.prompt: After ₹2,000 transport cost you earned ₹34,000 — ₹6,000 more than the middleman offer!
mp_2b.lesson: Transporting to the mandi took extra effort but yielded 21% more income. Collective transport with other farmers reduces cost further.

mp_2c.prompt: Prices fell further. You paid ₹1,500 storage and still sold for ₹1,400.
mp_2c.lesson: Storing grain requires proper facilities and market intelligence. Without these, waiting often leads to losses.

dp_1.prompt: You receive an SMS: 'Your Kisan Credit card is blocked. Share your OTP to reactivate.' What do you do?
dp_1.voicePrompt: You received an SMS. Your card is blocked. Share your OTP to reactivate. What do you do?

options.B: Ignore the SMS — call your bank directly
options.C: Ask a family member for advice first

dp_2a.prompt: You were scammed! ₹20,000 was withdrawn from your account. Banks never ask for OTPs.
dp_2a.lesson: NEVER share your OTP, PIN, or password. Banks and government schemes will NEVER ask for these. Report fraud to 1930 (National Cybercrime Helpline).

dp_2b.prompt: Smart! The bank confirmed it was a fraud attempt. Your account is safe.
dp_2b.lesson: [Skill Tested: Fraud Detection] Always verify by calling your bank's official number (back of debit card). Real banks NEVER ask for OTP via SMS or calls.

dp_2c.prompt: Your family member recognized it as a scam. Good thinking to ask!
dp_2c.lesson: When in doubt, consult trusted people before acting. Community knowledge is a powerful shield against fraud.

glossary.insurance: Protection against financial loss from crop failure.
glossary.loan: Money borrowed that must be paid back with interest.
glossary.savings: Money set aside for future emergencies.
glossary.interest: The cost of borrowing money or the reward for saving it.
glossary.kharif: Autumn harvest season, dependent on monsoon rains.
glossary.rabi: Spring harvest season, relies on irrigation.
